items.answer: The invisible man entered into a big London store. When the store was closed, he broke open the boxes and put on warm clothes. Only then he became visible.

items.answer: He was wandering the streets to get rid of the two boys who were following his footprints. He had set fire to the house and was homeless. Read And Find Out - 2

items.stem: What curious episode occure in the study ?
items.answer: The clergyman and his wife awoke to hear noises in the study. They heard the chink of money being taken from the drawer. They flung open the door. But they were amused to find the room empty. No body was there yet the drawer was opened and the money was missing. It was the curious episode.

items.stem: What other extraordinary things happen at the inn ?
items.answer: The extraordinary things happened at the inn are (a) The bedroom chair of the scientist became alive. It attacked Mrs. Hall and then pushed her and her husband out of the room. Then it slammed and locked the room. (b) The scientist appeared from his empty bedroom. (c) The scientist became first a headless man and then completely invisibly by throwing off his clothes. Think About It

items.stem: ‘Griffin was rather a lawless person.’ Comment.
items.answer: Griffin was not a true scientist as he misused his scientific discovery. Once he had a quarrel with his landlord. He had to eject Griffin. In revenge Griffin set fire to the house. To get away without being seen, he had to remove his clothes. Thus he became a homeless wanderer, without clothes, without money and quite invisible. He decided to steal money from the clergyman’s house. He made himself invisible and entered his study. The clergyman and his wife woke-up, when they heard noise in their study. They heard the chunk of money being stolen from the desk. They opened the door with a poker but there was no trace of the burglar. Griffin misued his scientific discovery without making benefit to the mankind.

items.stem: How would you assess Griffin as a scientist ?
items.answer: Griffin was a brilliant scientist. He had carried out a number of experiments to develop (technique) of making human body transparent and making it invisible. He swallowed rare drugs and his body became transparent. He could have easily used this knowledge of his for betterment of society but rather he was a lawless scientist. He hit the shopkeeper and stole his money. At the inn he entered the clergyman’s study and stole money from his desk. Thus he proved to be an eccentric scientist who used his scientific knowledge for wrong doings and posed a threat to the society. He misused his scientific discovery. We can call him stupid, false and a childish scientist. Talk About It

items.stem: Would you like to become invisible ? What advantages and disadvantages do you foresee, if you did ?
items.answer: Yes, becoming invisible can both be a curse as well as a boon. I would love to become invisible as this would give me a chance to face the difficulties and joys of life. If even I become invisible I would try to use this for spreading message of peace over humanity. If I realise that I can scatter wealth to help the poor even if it is at the cost of rich people, I would feel delighted. At times invisibility can be a great help to spy over the enemies and to catch the culprits.

items.stem: Are there forces around us that are invisible, for example, magnetism? Are there aspects of matter that are “invisible” or not visible to the naked eye ? What would the world be like if you could see such forces or such aspects of matter ?
items.answer: There are many forces around us that are invisible. For example, magnetism or the gravitational force is the force which we can feel but cannot see. It is the existence of such a force which has held the planets in their respective position and make the things fall to the earth. Had these forces not existed we would have been floating in the atmosphere. Some heavenly bodies can be seen with the help of the naked eye. While there are some stars which cannot be seen with the help of naked eyes. Such stars are so far off that visibility is not possible. If we could see such forces then the world would be surrounded by various rays which will be crossing each other like a maze. The confusion will be so great that one will not be able to understand which path to follow or which is restricted.

items.stem: What makes glass or water transparent (what is the scientific explanation for this)? Do you think it would be scientifically possible for a man to become invisible, or transparent ? (Keep in mind that writers of science fiction have often turned out to be prophetic in their imagination!)
items.answer: Glass or water are substances in which the molecules are not rigid. Such flexibility in the molecules gives them ability of free movement. When they move freely cohesive forces are weakened. Such an aspect makes them invisible or transparent. The man becoming invisible is just a figment of imagination. It would not be possible and can just be imagined and felt. There are some things. We can feel but can’t see. Scientifically it would not be possible for a man to be invisible. It is like we imagine. We have wings of fancy and touch the limitless horizons and soar higher. But these are just thought which have made-us believe that we are soaring higher but actually we are on the gound. So this is just a kind of hypnotism of our feelings and thoughts.

items.stem: Why did Griffin go inside a big London store ?
items.answer: Griffin went inside a big London store to gain some warmth, find a place for the night, and also to put on some clothes.

items.stem: Why were the two boys surprised when they saw the imprints of a pair of bare feet ?
items.answer: The two boys could see muddy footprints on the steps of a house in central London, descending towards the street. It was surprising to see the footprints without seeing anybody making them.

items.stem: How did Griffin try to get rid of Mrs. Hall’s accusations?
items.answer: Griffin got furious with Mrs. Hall’s accusation of stealing money and of not paying her rent. He threw off his bandages, spectacles and became invisible. He hit everyone and escaped from there.

items.stem: Why did Griffin set the landlord’s house on fire ?
items.answer: Griffin was not liked by his landlord. He decided to take revenge on him, so one day he set his house on fire. Moreover, he did not want anyone to know about his secret discovery.

items.stem: How did Griffin escape from the London store ?
items.answer: When two attendants of the store discovered Griffin, they chased him. Hence, in order to protect himself he threw away his clothes and became invisible and escaped from the London store.

items.stem: Why were the landlord and his wife surprised to see the scientist’s door open ?
items.answer: They were surprised because typically the door to the scientist’s room was shut and locked, and he would be very angry if anyone entered it.

items.stem: Why did Griffin not get a suitable house to live in ?
items.answer: Griffin was a lawless person, who was largely disliked by all. When his landlord tried to evict him, he set fire to the house, and escaped due to his invisibility. Thereafter, it became difficult for him to find a proper place to live in.

items.stem: How did Griffin try to become visible?
items.answer: Griffin went into a shop in Drury Lane, the heart of the theatre world, with the aim of finding something to wear, and becoming visible. He emerged from the shop wearing bandages around his forehead, dark glasses, a false nose, bushy sideburns and a large hat.

items.stem: Why was Mrs. Hall angry with Griffin, the strange scientist ?
items.answer: Griffin had attacked Mr. and Mrs. Hall and even threw her mother’s chair at her. Moreover, Griffm had not paid the rent for a long time. This made Mrs. Hall angry.

items.stem: What kind of discovery had Griffin made ? What was Griffin’s nature ?
items.answer: Griffin was a brilliant scientist. He had made an unusual discovery due to which a man could become invisible. But, at the same time, he was short-tempered, selfish and engaged in unlawful activities. He had set his landlord’s house on fire and hit the shopkeeper and the policeman just for his own selfish needs and gains.

items.stem: What reasons does Griffin give to Mrs. Hall for coming to Iping ?
items.answer: Griffin remained secluded in the village of Iping. He did not speak and mix with anybody in the village. He told Mrs. Hall that he wanted solitude and did not wish to be disturbed in his work. He further added that an accident had affected his face so he should just be left alone.

items.stem: Did Griffin reciprocate when Mrs. Hall wanted to be friendly with him ?
items.answer: No, Griffin was not keen to mix with people in the village of Iping. He told Mrs. Hall that his reason for coming to Iping was a desire for solitude. He even told her that he did not want to be disturbed in his work.

items.stem: Why was “the strange scientist strongly suspected of having had a hand” in the burglary at the clergyman’s home ?
items.answer: The news of the burglary at the clergyman’s home had become known throughout the village. The people of the village strongly suspected the strange scientist Griffin of having a hand in it. Moreover, he had suddenly produced some ready cash, when he had admitted not long before that he had no money anymore.

items.stem: What did Griffin do in the shop of a theatrical company ?
items.answer: Griffin wanted to conceal his identity and move away from London. So he entered the shop of a theatrical company, invisibly and wore bandages around his forehead. He even wore dark glasses, a false nose, big bushy side whiskers and a large brimmed hat to hide his appearance. After getting ready, he attacked the shopkeeper and ran away after taking all of his money.

items.stem: How did he save himself from the chasing staff of the store?
items.answer: Griffin took advantage of his being invisible and took shelter in a store at night. When Griffin saw that the salesmen of the store were coming near him, he took off all his clothes and became invisible. He did not have any other choice to save himself.

items.stem: What happened when Griffin didn’t wake up in time?
items.answer: Griffin did not wake up in time and when he saw the assistants at the shop approaching the next morning, he just panicked and ran. They gave him a chase and he could escape only after he took off his clothes. So, he was once again out in the open without clothes in the chilly air of January.

items.stem: Why did Mrs. Hall ignore Griffin’s strange habits?
items.answer: Mrs. Hall ignored Griffin’s strange habits because she was satisfied that her guest was an eccentric scientist and above all he had paid her in advance. Arrival of a stranger at an inn in winter was in any case an unusual even in Iping.

items.stem: Mr. Griffin entered the shop of the theatrical company. What did he do there?
items.answer: Mr. Griffin entered the shop to find clothes. He covered himself above his shoulders with bandages. He then wore dark glasses, a false nose and a large hat. He hit the shopkeeper and robbed him.

items.stem: A character arc is the transformation or development of a character throughout a story and refers to the changes a character undergoes as a result of his/her experiences, challenges and interactions with other characters. In light of the above information, trace the character arc of Griffin in H.G. Wells’ Footprints without Feet’.
items.answer: Griffin in H.G. Wells’ ‘Footprints without Feet’ undergoes a significant character arc throughout the story. Initially, he is portrayed as a brilliant yet eccentric scientist obsessed with achieving invisibility. However, as the narrative progresses, his obsession leads him down a path of moral degradation. Griffin’s character arc is marked by his descent into madness and amorality as he abuses his newfound power of invisibility for personal gain and revenge. By the end of the story, Griffin’s transformation is complete, culminating in his tragic demise as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and hubris.

items.stem: Imagine that Griffin’s conscience pricks him and he decides to write a diary entry, about misusing science and endangering society, in the context of his own experience. Write this diary entry, as Griffin, in about 120 words.
items.answer: 10 March 20XX, Monday 9:00 pm Dear Dairy, Today, as I reflect on my actions, I am overwhelmed by a profound sense of guilt and remorse. My pursuit of scientific discovery has led me down a dark path, blinding me to the ethical implications of my experiments. In my quest for power and invisibility, I have misused science to satisfy my own selfish desires, heedless of the consequences for society. My actions have endangered countless lives and unleashed chaos upon the world. The weight of my transgressions bears heavily upon my conscience, and I am haunted by the realization that I have become the very monster I sought to create. I can only hope that future generations will learn from my mistakes and wield science responsibly, for the betterment of humankind. Griffin

items.stem: Did Griffin from ‘Footprints without Feet’ follow the saying ‘With great power comes great responsibility’? Justify your answer in 120 words.
items.answer: No, Griffin did not follow the saying ‘with great power comes great responsibility’. Since Griffin did not think of anyone else except himself, this saying is not what he followed. After he managed to make himself invisible, he did not use his powers of invisibility for good. Instead, one of the first things he did was set fire to his landlord’s house in an act of revenge. He did not think of helping anyone with his newfound powers; instead, he harmed other people for his own gain. He stole clothes and food for himself without feeling any remorse. When his money ran low once more, he again resorted to stealing and robbed a clergyman. Finally, when the police were about to catch him, instead of going quietly and accepting his arrest, he fought back and escaped. At no time did Griffin take any responsibility for his actions.

items.stem: How did the invisible scientist first become visible? What compelled him to become invisible again in the chilly air of January?
items.answer: The invisible scientist first became visible when he slipped into a big London store for warmth from the bitterly cold weather. There he broke open boxes and wrappers and fitted himself into warm clothes. Fully dressed he was now also a fully visible person. Finally he settled down to sleep but he did not manage to get up on time, before the shop assistants arrived. Seeing them approach Griffin panicked and began to run. The shop assistants began chasing him and he could only escape by quickly taking off his newly found clothes. So once more he became invisible in the chilly January air.

items.stem: Mrs. Hall found the scientist rather eccentric. How can he be helped to lead a normal life ? Highlight the values that can help him become a better person.
items.answer: Griffin was an eccentric scientist who had come to Ping in a desire for solitude. He did not wish to be disturbed and moreover, he had come to the town at that time of winter when no one comes. Mrs. Hall found him eccentric also because of his looks. He was over dressed with all parts of his body covered. He was wearing dark glasses, big bushy side whiskers and a large hat all the time, even at night. He could be helped to lead a normal life by guiding him patiently. He should be counselled to work for the welfare of the society. The values of empathy, social responsibility, kindness, helpfulness, honesty to his profession, generosity can help Griffin to become a better person.

items.stem: What did the scientist do when he became furious? What happened to the constable and the people at the bar?
items.answer: When the scientist was furious, in anger he threw off bandages, whiskers, spectacles and all other worn costumes over the shoulders and became a headless man. The people in the bar were horrified because they found themselves staring at a headless man. The constable tried to arrest the scientist. He threw off his clothes one by one in order to become invisible. After sometime he could not be seen at all. Then the constable was trying to get hold of the invisible scientist. Some people tried to help him, but found themselves getting back blows which seemed to come from nowhere. At the end, the constable was knocked down unconscious by the scientist.

items.stem: How did the scientist look when he came to the inn? Give examples to show that he was a man of irritable temperament.
items.answer: The scientist came to the inn with an uncommon appearance. He had bandages around his forehead. He had put on dark glasses and had also put a false nose with big bushy side whiskers and was wearing a large hat. The scientist was indeed a man with an irritable temper because he foiled all of Mrs Hall’s attempts to be friendly with him and told her that he had no desire to talk. His irritable temper also forced him to tell Mrs Hall that he wanted solitude and did not wish to be disturbed in his work.

items.stem: Imagine that you are Jaffers, the village constable. Write a letter to your wife Isabel telling about your encounter with an invisible man.
items.answer: Police Quarters, Iping, U.K. 7 December, 20xx My dear Isabel, Today I had a very strange experience. It has never happened in my life before. Can you believe me if I say that today I had an encounter with a man, who threw off his clothes one by one, and became invisible. It happened just before my own eyes. The man who turned invisible was a strange scientist who had hired two rooms at the village inn. He was suspected of having stolen clergyman’s money from his house. Today, I had gone to arrest him with the magistrate’s warrant. I fought bravely, but he took advantage of his invisibility. I was hit by so many unseen blows that I soon became unconscious. He knocked me down and escaped. Yours affectionately, Jaffers

items.stem: Describe the scene which took place after the arrival of Mr. Jaffers, the constable, in the story ‘Footprints Without Feet’. Or Describe the scene when Mr. Jaffers tries ‘to arrest a man without head’.
items.answer: Mr. Jaffers, the constable, arrived and he was quite surprised to find that he had to arrest a man without a head. But it does not matter. There followed a remarkable scene as the policeman tried to get hold of a man who was becoming more and more invisible as he was taking off one garment after another. Finally the constable found himself struggling with someone invisible. Some people tried to help him, but found themselves hit by blows that seemed to come from nowhere. In the end the constable was knocked unconscious as he made a last attempt to hold on to the Invisible scientist.
